title: Correlative Microscopy to Reveal Origins of Dislocation Luminescence in Diamond
content: Diamond is an exciting material for a variety of device applications – among them, quantum sensing and computing, power electronics, and radiation detection [1, 2]. To achieve high-performing devices requires controlling and mitigating dislocations: defects that arise from interface damage or contamination in homoepitaxial growth and from lattice misfit in heteroepitaxy on larger substrates [3, 4]. By understanding dislocation properties, we can develop techniques to rapidly assess dislocations and their generation mechanisms.
